conservation.condition_narrative: Generally, the support, structure, and design layers are seen to be secure and stable. Aggregated areas of foxing spots, as well as more isolated instances of foxing, generally occur throughout the entire work. Tears have been previously repaired. The complex of creases is a result of Georgia O'Keeffe's storage and travel campaigns and has been allowed to generally remain intact. There is a loose wood accretion that can migrate in handling, currently located in the bottom right corner of the mat window.
conservation.technical_description:
**Support:** The support is a very thin, cream-colored, smooth-surfaced, translucent, wove paper. The sheet edges appear commercially cut, but the bottom right corner is uneven as a result of the artist's storage and handling creases. 
 
  
 
**Ground or Support Preparation:** The paper surface appears to have an original commercial sizing, but there is no indication of any other surface preparation by the artist. 
 
 
 
**Design Layers:** The artist drew pencil graphite lines in single, continuous, and connected forms to create outlines of the major forms of the Ranchos de Taos Church. There are no shading applications of media to indicate volumetric form or shadow. A rectangular framing outline is drawn surrounding the central form, indicating the general ratio, vertical to horizontal, of a future painting. In script, near the lower, viewer-left corner, the artist has written "Ranchos Church 29" and "Phillips." 
 
 
 
**Surface Coating:** None. 
 
 
 
**Framing, Backing, and Hanging Hardware:** The work is matted in 100% cotton Rising Museum Board with a 4-ply backing and an 8-ply window over-mat. The work is backed with Microchamber xeolite–charcoal corrugated board and faced with Optium 3mm, tin-Ti optically coated acrylic glazing.
